{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01SF8JBFyWE9hF6dhJN7a2J2","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t\"\"\"HTTP routes for books: add a book from a form post, and list stored books in the order added.\"\"\"\n2\t\n3\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n4\t\n5\tfrom flask import Blueprint, current_app, jsonify, redirect, render_template, request\n6\tfrom werkzeug.wrappers import Response\n7\t\n8\tfrom persistence import Database\n9\t\n10\tfrom .book_service import BookRejected, add_book, list_books\n11\t\n12\tbp = Blueprint(\"books\", __name__)\n13\t\n14\t\n15\tdef _database() -> Database:\n16\t    return current_app.extensions[\"database\"]\n17\t\n18\t\n19\t@bp.get(\"/books\")\n20\tdef get_books() -> Response:\n21\t    \"\"\"Return every stored book as a JSON array of ``id``, ``title`` and ``author``, oldest first.\"\"\"\n22\t    return jsonify(\n23\t        [{\"id\": row.id, \"title\": row.title, \"author\": row.author} for row in list_books(_database())]\n24\t    )\n25\t\n26\t\n27\t@bp.post(\"/books\")\n28\tdef create_book() -> Response:\n29\t    \"\"\"Add a book from the ``title`` and ``author`` form fields, then redirect to the start page.\"\"\"\n30\t    title = request.form.get(\"title\", \"\").strip()\n31\t    author = request.form.get(\"author\", \"\").strip()\n32\t    try:\n33\t of ``id``, ``title`` and ``author``, oldest first.\"\"\"\n    return jsonify(\n        [{\"id\": row.id, \"title\": row.title, \"author\": row.author} for row in list_books(_database())]\n    )\n\n\n@bp.post(\"/books\")\ndef create_book() -> Response:\n    \"\"\"Add a book from the ``title`` and ``author`` form fields, then redirect to the start page.\"\"\"\n    title = {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_015eFYXtcNy92Y7rbPhhFmev","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t\"\"\"Book behavior for the ReadingList web application, free of any Flask dependency.\"\"\"\n2\t\n3\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n4\t\n5\tfrom persistence import Database\n6\tfrom persistence.schema import BookRow\n7\t\n8\t\n9\tclass BookRejected(ValueError):\n10\t    \"\"\"A submission the application refuses to store; ``reason`` says why.\"\"\"\n11\t\n12\t    def __init__(self, reason: str) -> None:\n13\t        super().__init__(reason)\n14\t        self.reason = reason\n15\t\n16\t\n17\tdef add_book(database: Database, title: str, author: str) -> BookRow:\n18\t    \"\"\"Store a book appended after every existing book and return the stored row.\n19\t\n20\t    Values are expected already trimmed by the caller. An empty title or author is refused\n21\t    without touching the store, so a stored book always has both.\n22\t    \"\"\"\n23\t    if not title:\n24\t        raise BookRejected(\"rejected: title is empty\")\n25\t    if not author:\n26\t        raise BookRejected(\"rejected: author is empty\")\n27\t    return database.books.create(title=title, author=author)\n28\t\n29\t\n30\tdef list_books(database: Database) -> list[BookRow]:\n31\t    \"\"\"Return every stored book in the order added, oldest first.\n32\t\n33\t    The order is enforced here, by ascending id, rather than trusted to the store's select, which\n34\t    the generated persistence layer issues without an ORDER BY clause.\n35\t    \"\"\"\n36\t    return sorted(database.books.list(), key=lambda row: row.id)\n37\t"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"9eef8fcf-938b-4ea7-a3b6-83ab591d92fb","uuid":"9bf44697-897d-4b7c-a11a-92940ff0a3da","timestamp":"2026-10-23T15:01:49.067Z","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/ReadingList/runs/20261023.144538/build/ReadingList/app_server/book_service.py","content":"\"\"\"Book behavior for the ReadingList web application, free of any Flask dependency.\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom persistence import Database\nfrom persistence.schema import BookRow\n\n\nclass BookRejected(ValueError):\n    \"\"\"A submission the application refuses to store; ``reason`` says why.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, reason: str) -> None:\n        super().__init__(reason)\n        self.reason = reason\n\n\ndef add_book(database: Database, title: str, author: str) -> BookRow:\n    \"\"\"Store a book appended after every existing book and return the stored row.\n\n    Values are expected already trimmed by the caller. An empty title or author is refused\n    without touching the store, so a stored book always has both.\n    \"\"\"\n    if not title:\n        raise BookRejected(\"rejected: title is empty\")\n    if not author:\n        raise BookRejected(\"rejected: author is empty\")\n    return database.books.create(title=title, author=author)\n\n\ndef list_books(database: Database) -> list[BookRow]:\n    \"\"\"Return every stored book in the order added, oldest first.\n\n    The order is enforced here, by ascending id, rather than trusted to the store's select, which\n    the generated persistence layer issues without an ORDER BY clause.\n    \"\"\"\n    return sorted(database.books.list(), key=lambda row: row.id)\n","numLines":37,"startLine":1,"totalLines":37}},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_015eFYXtcNy92Y7rbPhhFmev","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

add_book\n9\t\n10\tPROJECT_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent\n11\t\n12\t\n13\t@pytest.fixture\n14\tdef app(monkeypatch, tmp_path):\n15\t    \"\"\"A fresh application over its own store, so no test touches the configured data/app.db.\"\"\"\n16\t    store = tmp_path / \"add-book.db\"\n17\t    monkeypatch.setenv(\"DATABASE_URL\", f\"sqlite:///{store}\")\n18\t    monkeypatch.delenv(\"DATABASE_PATH\", raising=False)\n19\t    application = create_app()\n20\t    application.extensions[\"database\"].execute_script((PROJECT_ROOT / \"schema.sql\").read_text())\n21\t    return application\n22\t\n23\t\n24\tdef _stored(app) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:\n25\t    \"\"\"Read every stored book back through the persistence package, in order added.\"\"\"\n26\t    return [(row.title, row.author) for row in app.extensions[\"database\"].books.list()]\n27\t\n28\t\n29\tdef test_valid_submission_redirects_with_303_to_start_page(app):\n30\t    response = app.test_client().post(\"/books\", data={\"title\": \"Dune\", \"author\": \"Frank Herbert\"})\n31\t\n32\t    assert response.status_code == 303\n33\t    assert response.headers[\"Location\"] == \"/\"\n34\t\n35\t\n36\tdef test_valid_submission_stores_title_and_author(app):\n37\t    app.test_client().post(\"/books\", data={\"title\": \"Dune\", \"author\": \"Frank Herbert\"})\n38\t\n39\t    assert _stored(app) == [(\"Dune\", \"Frank Herbert\")]\n40\t\n41\t\n42\tdef test_surrounding_whitespace_is_trimmed_before_storing(app):\n43\t    app.test_client().post(\"/books\", data={\"title\": \" app.test_client().post(\"/books\", data={\"title\": \"Dune  Messiah\", \"author\": \"Frank  Herbert\"})\n50\t\n51\t    assert _stored(app) == [(\"Dune  Messiah\", \"Frank for ``get``, ``list``, and ``delete`` they\n68\t    are the predicate, and for ``create`` and ``update`` they are the values written. ``row`` is\n69\t    the dataclass a read or a create returns, and ``columns`` are the columns it selects.\n70\t    \"\"\"\n71\t\n72\t    identifier: str\n73\t    table: str\n74\t    verb: str\n75\t    inputs: tuple[str, ...]\n76\t    row: type | None = None\n77\t    columns: tuple[str, ...] = ()\n78\t    key: str | None = None\n79\t\n80\t\n81\t@dataclass(frozen=True)\n82\tclass Schema:\n83\t    \"\"\"The generated declaration: every table and every operation reaching one.\"\"\"\n84\t\n85\t    tables: tuple[Table, ...]\n86\t    operations: tuple[Operation, ...]\n87\t\n88\t    def by_table(self) -> dict[str, tuple[Operation, ...]]:\n89\t        grouped: dict[str, list[Operation]] = {table.name: [] for table in self.tables}\n90\t        for operation in self.operations:\n91\t            grouped.setdefault(operation.table, []).append(operation)\n92\t        return {name: tuple(items) for name, items in grouped.items()}\n93\t\n94\t\n95\tclass Driver:\n96\t    \"\"\"Statement construction shared by every engine.\n97\t\n98\t    Subclasses supply connection handling and the two things engines genuinely disagree about:\n99\t    how a parameter is spelled, and how a freshly inserted row reports its key. Everything else is\n100\t    identical SQL, so it is written once here rather than twice in the engines.\n101\t    \"\"\"\n102\t\n103\t    def prepare_schema(self, sql: str) -> str:\n104\t        \"\"\"Translate generated DDL for this engine.\"\"\"\n105\t        return sql\n106\t\n107\t    #: Spelled by the DB-API driver, not by this class's callers.\n108\t    paramstyle = \"qmark\"\n109\t    returning = False\n110\t\n111\t    def connect(self) -> Any:  # pragma: no cover - engine specific\n112\t        raise NotImplementedError\n113\t\n114\t    def close(self) -> None:  # pragma: no cover - engine specific\n115\t        raise NotImplementedError\n116\t\n117\t    def placeholder(self, index: int) -> str:\n118\t        \"\"\"Render parameter ``index`` (0-based) in this engine's spelling.\"\"\"\n119\t        return \"?\" if self.paramstyle == \"qmark\" else \"%s\"\n120\t\n121\t    @staticmethod\n122\t    def quote(identifier: str) -> str:\n123\t        \"\"\"Quote a declared identifier. Never called with caller-supplied text.\"\"\"\n124\t        if not identifier.replace(\"_\", \"\").isalnum():\n125\t            raise PersistenceError(f\"refusing unsafe identifier f\"{self.quote(name)} = {self.placeholder(start + offset)}\"\n131\t            for offset, name in enumerate(names)\n132\t        )\n133\t\n134\t    def select(self, table: str, columns: {self.quote(table)}\"\n137\t        if predicate:\n138\t            statement += f\" WHERE {self._predicate(predicate)}\"\n139\t        return statement\n140\t\n141\t    def insert(self, table: str, NotImplementedError\n166\t\n167\t\n168\tclass TableAccess:\n169\t    \"\"\"The methods one table grants, bound from the declaration rather than defined by hand.\"\"\"\n170\t\n171\t    def __init__(self, table: Table, operations: Iterable[Operation], database: Database) -> None:\n172\t        self._table = table\n173\t        self._database = database\n174\t        self._operations = Connection\n195\t    handling is internal and may change without affecting any caller.\n196\t    \"\"\"\n197\t\n198\t    def __init__(self, dsn: str, schema: Schema, *, driver: Driver | None = None) -> None:\n199\t        self._rollback_owner = None\n200\t        self._schema = schema\n201\t        self._driver = driver if driver is not None else open_driver(dsn)\n202\t        grouped = schema.by_table()\n203\t        for table in schema.tables:\n204\t            setattr(self, table.name, TableAccess(table, grouped.get(table.name, ()), self))\n205\t\n206\t    @property\n207\t    def driver(self) -> Driver:\n208\t        if self._rollback_owner is not None:\n209\t            raise PersistenceError(\"driver access is forbidden inside a rollback session\")\n210\t        return self._driver\n211\t\n212\t    def close(self) -> None:\n213\t        if self._rollback_owner is not None:\n214\t            raise PersistenceError(\"the rollback session owns connection lifetime\")\n215\t        self._driver.close()\n216\t\n217\t    @contextmanager\n218\t    def rollback_session(self):\n219\t        \"\"\"Use this connection for setup, behavior and assertions; always roll back.\n220\t\n221\t        Normal calls remain autocommitted. No schema creation, nested transaction,\n222\t        driver escape, or cross-thread operation is allowed in this scope.\n223\t        \"\"\"\n224\t        if self._rollback_owner is not None:\n225\t            raise PersistenceError(\"nested rollback session\")\n226\t        connection = self._driver.connect()\n227\t        cursor = connection.cursor()\n228\t        try:\n229\t            cursor.execute(\"BEGIN\")\n230\t            self._rollback_owner = threading.get_ident()\n231\t            try:\n232\t                yield self\n233\t            finally:\n234\t                try:\n235\t                    cursor.execute(\"ROLLBACK\")\n236\t                except Exception as exc:\n237\t                    raise PersistenceError(f\"acceptance rollback failed: {exc}\") from exc\n238\t                finally:\n239\t                    self._rollback_owner = None\n240\t        finally:\n241\t            cursor.close()\n242\t            self._driver.close()\n243\t\n244\t\n245\t    def __enter__(self) -> Database:\n246\t        return self\n247\t\n248\t    def __exit__(self, *_: object) -> None:\n249\t        self.close()\n250\t\n251\t    def execute_script(self, sql: str) -> None:\n252\t        \"\"\"Apply generated DDL. The schema is built once, at the DATABASE build step.\"\"\"\n253\t        if self._rollback_owner is not None:\n254\t            raise PersistenceError(\"schema and transaction SQL are forbidden in rollback sessions\")\n255\t        cursor = self._open(\"schema\")\n256\t        try:\n257\t            for statement in statements(self._driver.prepare_schema(sql)):\n258\t                cursor.execute(statement)\n259\t        finally:\n260\t            cursor.close()\n261\t\n262\t    def run(self, operation: Operation, arguments: Mapping[str, Any]) -> Any:\n263\t        \"\"\"Execute one declared operation with bound parameters.\"\"\"\n264\t        unknown = sorted(set(arguments) - set(operation.inputs))\n265\t        if unknown:\n266\t            raise PersistenceError(\n267\t                f\"{operation.identifier} does not accept {', '.join(unknown)}. Declared inputs: \"\n268\t                f\"{', '.join(operation.inputs) or 'none'}.\"\n269\t            )\n270\t        if operation not in self._schema.operations:\n271\t            raise UnknownOperation(f\"{operation.identifier} is not a declared operation\")\n272\t        key = operation.key or self._primary_key(operation.table)\n273\t        if operation.verb in (\"get\", \"update\", \"delete\") and key in operation.inputs and key not in arguments:\n274\t            raise PersistenceError(f\"{operation.identifier} requires key {key}\")\n275\t        if operation.verb == \"delete\" and not arguments:\n276\t            raise PersistenceError(f\"{operation.identifier} requires a delete predicate\")\n277\t        names = [name for name in operation.inputs if name in arguments]\n278\t        values = [arguments[name] for name in names]\n279\t        cursor = self._open(operation.identifier)\n280\t        try:\n281\t            if self._rollback_owner is not None:\n282\t                cursor.execute(\"SAVEPOINT drydock_operation\")\n283\t            result = self._dispatch(operation, cursor, names, values)\n284\t            if self._rollback_owner is not None:\n285\t                cursor.execute(\"RELEASE SAVEPOINT drydock_operation\")\n286\t            return result\n287\t        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - translated at the boundary on purpose\n288\t            if self._rollback_owner is not None:\n289\t                cursor.execute(\"ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT drydock_operation\")\n290\t                cursor.execute(\"RELEASE SAVEPOINT drydock_operation\")\n291\t            raise PersistenceError(f\"{operation.identifier} failed: {exc}\") from exc\n292\t        finally:\n293\t            cursor.close()\n294\t\n295\t    def _open(self, action: str) -> Any:\n296\t        \"\"\"Return a cursor, translating a refused or failed connection.\"\"\"\n297\t        if self._rollback_owner not in (None, threading.get_ident()):\n298\t            raise PersistenceError(\"rollback session requires its owning thread and connection\")\n299\t        try:\n300\t            return self._driver.connect().cursor()\n301\t        except PersistenceError:\n302\t            raise\n303\t        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - A supplied key\n328\t            # wins over the engine's report: SQLite's lastrowid is the rowid, not a text key.\n329\t            if key is None:\n330\t                return self._build(operation, names, values)\n331\t            if key in names:\n332\t                identity = values[names.index(key)]\n333\t            columns = operation.columns or self._columns(table)\n334\t            cursor.execute(self._driver.select(table, columns, [key]), [identity])\n335\t            return self._build(operation, columns, cursor.fetchone())\n336\t        if verb == \"update\":\n337\t Identifiers cannot be\nbound in any engine, so they are taken only from the generated schema — which Drydock validated\nagainst ``^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`` before emitting it — and are quoted on the way out.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom collections.abc import Callable, Iterable, Mapping, Sequence\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, fields\nfrom contextlib import contextmanager\nimport threading\nfrom typing import Any\n\n__all__ = [\n    \"Database\",\n    \"Driver\",\n    \"Operation\",\n    \"PersistenceError\",\n    \"Schema\",\n    \"Table\",\n    \"statements\",\n    \"UnknownOperation\",\n]\n\nVERBS = (\"get\", \"list\", \"create\", \"update\", \"delete\")\n\n\nclass PersistenceError(RuntimeError):\n    \"\"\"A persistence failure the caller may act on, raised in place of a driver exception.\"\"\"\n\n\nclass UnknownOperation(PersistenceError):\n    \"\"\"A verb was requested that the declaration does not grant for that table.\"\"\"\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Table:\n    \"\"\"One declared table: its columns and the column that identifies a row.\"\"\"\n\n    name: str\n    columns: tuple[str, ...]\n    primary_key: str | None = None\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Operation:\n    \"\"\"One declared access pattern, reduced to what executing it requires.\n\n    ``inputs`` are the parameters the caller supplies; for ``get``, ``list``, and ``delete`` they\n    are the predicate, and for ``create`` and ``update`` they are the values written. ``row`` is\n    the dataclass a read or a create returns, and ``columns`` are the columns it selects.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    identifier: str\n    table: str\n    verb: str\n    inputs: tuple[str, ...]\n    row: type | None = None\n    columns: tuple[str, ...] = ()\n    key: str | None = None\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Schema:\n    \"\"\"The generated declaration: every table and every operation reaching one.\"\"\"\n\n    tables: tuple[Table, ...]\n    operations: tuple[Operation, ...]\n\n    def by_table(self) -> dict[str, tuple[Operation, ...]]:\n        grouped: dict[str, list[Operation]] = {table.name: [] for table in self.tables}\n        for operation in self.operations:\n            grouped.setdefault(operation.table, []).append(operation)\n        return {name: tuple(items) for name, items in grouped.items()}\n\n\nclass Driver:\n    \"\"\"Statement construction shared by every engine.\n\n    Subclasses supply connection handling and the two things engines genuinely disagree about:\n    how a parameter is spelled, and how a freshly inserted row reports its key. Everything else is\n    identical SQL, so it is written once here rather than twice in the engines.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def prepare_schema(self, sql: str) -> str:\n        \"\"\"Translate generated DDL for this engine.\"\"\"\n        return sql\n\n    #: Spelled by the DB-API driver, not by this class's callers.\n    paramstyle = \"qmark\"\n    returning = False\n\n    def connect(self) -> Any:  # pragma: no cover - engine specific\n        raise NotImplementedError\n\n    def close(self) -> None:  # pragma: no cover - engine specific\n        raise NotImplementedError\n\n    def placeholder(self, index: int) -> str:\n        \"\"\"Render parameter ``index`` (0-based) in this engine's spelling.\"\"\"\n        return \"?\" if self.paramstyle == \"qmark\" else \"%s\"\n\n    @staticmethod\n    def quote(identifier: str) -> str:\n        \"\"\"Quote a declared identifier. Never called with caller-supplied text.\"\"\"\n        if not identifier.replace(\"_\", \"\").isalnum():\n            raise PersistenceError(f\"refusing unsafe identifier {identifier!r}\")\n        return f'\"{identifier}\"'\n\n    def _predicate(self, names: Sequence[str], start: int = 0) -> str:\n        return \" AND \".join(\n            f\"{self.quote(name)} = {self.placeholder(start + offset)}\"\n            for offset, name in enumerate(names)\n        )\n\n    def select(self, table: str, columns: Sequence[str], predicate: Sequence[str]) -> str:\n        selected = \", \".join(self.quote(name) for name in columns)\n        statement = f\"SELECT {selected} FROM {self.quote(table)}\"\n        if predicate:\n            statement += f\" WHERE {self._predicate(predicate)}\"\n        return statement\n\n    def insert(self, table: str, columns: Sequence[str], key: str | None) -> str:\n        names = \", \".join(self.quote(name) for name in columns)\n        marks = \", \".join(self.placeholder(index) for index in range(len(columns)))\n        statement = f\"INSERT INTO {self.quote(table)} ({names}) VALUES ({marks})\"\n        if self.returning and key:\n            statement += f\" RETURNING {self.quote(key)}\"\n        return statement\n\n    def update(self, table: str, columns: Sequence[str], predicate: Sequence[str]) -> str:\n        assignments = \", \".join(\n            f\"{self.quote(name)} = {self.placeholder(index)}\" for index, name in enumerate(columns)\n        )\n        statement = f\"UPDATE {self.quote(table)} SET {assignments}\"\n        if predicate:\n            statement += f\" WHERE {self._predicate(predicate, len(columns))}\"\n        return statement\n\n    def delete(self, table: str, predicate: Sequence[str]) -> str:\n        statement = f\"DELETE FROM {self.quote(table)}\"\n        if predicate:\n            statement += f\" WHERE {self._predicate(predicate)}\"\n        return statement\n\n    def inserted_key(self, cursor: Any) -> Any:  # pragma: no cover - engine specific\n        raise NotImplementedError\n\n\nclass TableAccess:\n    \"\"\"The methods one table grants, bound from the declaration rather than defined by hand.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, table: Table, operations: Iterable[Operation], database: Database) -> None:\n        self._table = table\n        self._database = database\n        self._operations = {operation.verb: operation for operation in operations}\n\n    def __repr__(self) -> str:\n        granted = \", \".join(sorted(self._operations))\n        return f\"<TableAccess {self._table.name}: {granted or 'no declared operation'}>\"\n\n    def __getattr__(self, verb: str) -> Callable[..., Any]:\n        operation = self._operations.get(verb)\n        if operation is None:\n            granted = \", \".join(sorted(self._operations)) or \"none\"\n            raise UnknownOperation(\n                f\"{self._table.name} declares no {verb!r} operation. Declared: {granted}. \"\n                \"Add an access pattern to DATABASE.md rather than reaching around this class.\"\n            )\n        return lambda **arguments: self._database.run(operation, arguments)\n\n\nclass Database:\n    \"\"\"One store, presented to callers as declared tables with declared methods.\n\n    Callers construct one instance, share it freely, and call methods synchronously. Connection\n    handling is internal and may change without affecting any caller.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, dsn: str, schema: Schema, *, driver: Driver | None = None) -> None:\n        self._rollback_owner = None\n        self._schema = schema\n        self._driver = driver if driver is not None else open_driver(dsn)\n        grouped = schema.by_table()\n        for table in schema.tables:\n            setattr(self, table.name, TableAccess(table, grouped.get(table.name, ()), self))\n\n    @property\n    def driver(self) -> Driver:\n        if self._rollback_owner is not None:\n            raise PersistenceError(\"driver access is forbidden inside a rollback session\")\n        return self._driver\n\n    def close(self) -> None:\n        if self._rollback_owner is not None:\n            raise PersistenceError(\"the rollback session owns connection lifetime\")\n        self._driver.close()\n\n    @contextmanager\n    def rollback_session(self):\n        \"\"\"Use this connection for setup, behavior and assertions; always roll back.\n\n        Normal calls remain autocommitted. No schema creation, nested transaction,\n        driver escape, or cross-thread operation is allowed in this scope.\n        \"\"\"\n        if self._rollback_owner is not None:\n            raise PersistenceError(\"nested rollback session\")\n        connection = self._driver.connect()\n        cursor = connection.cursor()\n        try:\n            cursor.execute(\"BEGIN\")\n            self._rollback_owner = threading.get_ident()\n            try:\n                yield self\n            finally:\n                try:\n                    cursor.execute(\"ROLLBACK\")\n                except Exception as exc:\n                    raise PersistenceError(f\"acceptance rollback failed: {exc}\") from exc\n                finally:\n                    self._rollback_owner = None\n        finally:\n            cursor.close()\n            self._driver.close()\n\n\n    def __enter__(self) -> Database:\n        return self\n\n    def __exit__(self, *_: object) -> None:\n        self.close()\n\n    def execute_script(self, sql: str) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Apply generated DDL. The schema is built once, at the DATABASE build step.\"\"\"\n        if self._rollback_owner is not None:\n            raise PersistenceError(\"schema and transaction SQL are forbidden in rollback sessions\")\n        cursor = self._open(\"schema\")\n        try:\n            for statement in statements(self._driver.prepare_schema(sql)):\n                cursor.execute(statement)\n        finally:\n            cursor.close()\n\n    def run(self, operation: Operation, arguments: Mapping[str, Any]) -> Any:\n        \"\"\"Execute one declared operation with bound parameters.\"\"\"\n        unknown = sorted(set(arguments) - set(operation.inputs))\n        if unknown:\n            raise PersistenceError(\n                f\"{operation.identifier} does not accept {', '.join(unknown)}. Declared inputs: \"\n                f\"{', '.join(operation.inputs) or 'none'}.\"\n            )\n        if operation not in self._schema.operations:\n            raise UnknownOperation(f\"{operation.identifier} is not a declared operation\")\n        key = operation.key or self._primary_key(operation.table)\n        if operation.verb in (\"get\", \"update\", \"delete\") and key in operation.inputs and key not in arguments:\n            raise PersistenceError(f\"{operation.identifier} requires key {key}\")\n        if operation.verb == \"delete\" and not arguments:\n            raise PersistenceError(f\"{operation.identifier} requires a delete predicate\")\n        names = [name for name in operation.inputs if name in arguments]\n        values = [arguments[name] for name in names]\n        cursor = self._open(operation.identifier)\n        try:\n            if self._rollback_owner is not None:\n                cursor.execute(\"SAVEPOINT drydock_operation\")\n            result = self._dispatch(operation, cursor, names, values)\n            if self._rollback_owner is not None:\n                cursor.execute(\"RELEASE SAVEPOINT drydock_operation\")\n            return result\n        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - translated at the boundary on purpose\n            if self._rollback_owner is not None:\n                cursor.execute(\"ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT drydock_operation\")\n                cursor.execute(\"RELEASE SAVEPOINT drydock_operation\")\n            raise PersistenceError(f\"{operation.identifier} failed: {exc}\") from exc\n        finally:\n            cursor.close()\n\n    def _open(self, action: str) -> Any:\n        \"\"\"Return a cursor, translating a refused or failed connection.\"\"\"\n        if self._rollback_owner not in (None, threading.get_ident()):\n            raise PersistenceError(\"rollback session requires its owning thread and connection\")\n        try:\n            return self._driver.connect().cursor()\n        except PersistenceError:\n            raise\n        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - translated at the boundary on purpose\n            raise PersistenceError(f\"{action} could not connect: {exc}\") from exc\n\n    def _dispatch(\n        self,\n        operation: Operation,\n        cursor: Any,\n        names: list[str],\n        values: list[Any],\n    ) -> Any:\n        verb = operation.verb\n        table = operation.table\n        if verb in (\"get\", \"list\"):\n            columns = operation.columns or self._columns(table)\n            cursor.execute(self._driver.select(table, columns, names), values)\n            rows = cursor.fetchall() if verb == \"list\" else cursor.fetchmany(1)\n            built = [self._build(operation, columns, row) for row in rows]\n            return built if verb == \"list\" else (built[0] if built else None)\n        if verb == \"create\":\n            key = operation.key or self._primary_key(table)\n            cursor.execute(self._driver.insert(table, names, key), values)\n            identity = self._driver.inserted_key(cursor)\n            if operation.row is None:\n                return identity\n            # The declared Output row, read back so column defaults are included. A supplied key\n            # wins over the engine's report: SQLite's lastrowid is the rowid, not a text key.\n            if key is None:\n                return self._build(operation, names, values)\n            if key in names:\n                identity = values[names.index(key)]\n            columns = operation.columns or self._columns(table)\n            cursor.execute(self._driver.select(table, columns, [key]), [identity])\n            return self._build(operation, columns, cursor.fetchone())\n        if verb == \"update\":\n            key = operation.key or self._primary_key(table)\n            if key is None or key not in names:\n                raise PersistenceError(\n                    f\"{operation.identifier} updates {table} without supplying {key or 'a key'}\"\n                )\n            assigned = [name for name in names if name != key]\n            ordered = [values[names.index(name)] for name in assigned] + [values[names.index(key)]]\n            cursor.execute(self._driver.update(table, assigned, [key]), ordered)\n            return cursor.rowcount\n        if verb == \"delete\":\n            cursor.execute(self._driver.delete(table, names), values)\n            return cursor.rowcount\n        raise UnknownOperation(f\"{operation.identifier} names unsupported verb {verb!r}\")\n\n    def _columns(self, table: str) -> tuple[str, ...]:\n        for declared in self._schema.tables:\n            if declared.name == table:\n                return declared.columns\n        raise PersistenceError(f\"{table} is not a declared table\")\n\n    def _primary_key(self, table: str) -> str | None:\n        for declared in self._schema.tables:\n            if declared.name == table:\n                return declared.primary_key\n        return None\n\n    @staticmethod\n    def _build(operation: Operation, columns: Sequence[str], row: Sequence[Any]) -> Any:\n        if operation.row is None:\n            return dict(zip(columns, row, strict=False))\n        accepted = {field.name for field in fields(operation.row)}\n        return operation.row(**{\n            name: value for name, value in zip(columns, row, strict=False) if name in accepted\n        })\n\n\ndef statements(sql: str) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Split a DDL script into statements.\n\n    Comment lines are dropped and a semicolon inside a quoted literal does not end a statement —\n    a ``DEFAULT \\'a;b\\'`` would otherwise be cut in half, and the halves are not valid SQL.\n    \"\"\"\n    body = \"\\n\".join(line for line in sql.splitlines() if not line.lstrip().startswith(\"--\"))\n    parts: list[str] = []\n    current: list[str] = []\n    quoted = False\n    for character in body:\n        if character == \"'\":\n            quoted = not quoted\n        if character == \";\" and not quoted:\n            parts.append(\"\".join(current))\n            current = []\n            continue\n        current.append(character)\n    parts.append(\"\".join(current))\n    return [statement.strip() for statement in parts if statement.strip()]\n\n\ndef open_driver(dsn: str) -> Driver:\n    \"\"\"Select the engine from the DSN, so one build serves SQLite in test and Postgres in production.\"\"\"\n    scheme = dsn.split(\"://\", 1)[0].lower() if \"://\" in dsn else \"sqlite\"\n    if scheme in (\"postgres\", \"postgresql\"):\n        try:\n            from .postgres import PostgresDriver\n        except ImportError:  # flat layout\n            from postgres import PostgresDriver\n\n        return PostgresDriver(dsn)\n    if scheme in (\"sqlite\", \"file\") or \"://\" not in dsn:\n        try:\n            from .sqlite import SqliteDriver\n        except ImportError:  # flat layout\n            from sqlite import SqliteDriver\n\n        return SqliteDriver(dsn)\n    raise PersistenceError(\n        f\"no persistence driver for {scheme!r}. Drydock ships sqlite and postgres; add a driver \"\n        \"beside this file and a branch here for another engine.\"\n    )\n","numLines":416,"startLine":1,"totalLines":416}},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_01JLLuL2h1x1FSRhJc6ZV1h9","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

tmp_path):\n    \"\"\"Point the application at a fresh store per test, so listing starts from a known state.\"\"\"\n    url = f\"sqlite:///{tmp_path / 'list-books.db'}\"\n    monkeypatch.setenv(\"DATABASE_URL\", url)\n    monkeypatch.delenv(\"DATABASE_PATH\", raising=False)\n    with open_database(url) as database:\n        database.execute_script((PROJECT_ROOT / \"schema.sql\").read_text())\n    return url\n\n\ndef _add(client, title: str, author: str = \"List Author\") -> None:\n    assert client.post(\"/books\", data={\"title\": title, \"author\": author}).status_code == 303\n\n\ndef test_get_books_answers_200_with_json(web_client):\n    response = web_client.get(\"/books\")\n\n    assert response.status_code == 200\n    assert response.is_json\n\n\ndef test_empty_store_lists_empty_array(web_client):\n    assert web_client.get(\"/books\").get_json() == []\n\n\ndef test_single_book_is_listed_with_id_title_and_author(web_client):\n    _add(web_client, \"Dune\", \"Frank Herbert\")\n\n    body = web_client.get(\"/books\").get_json()\n\n    assert len(body) == 1\n    assert body[0][\"title\"] == \"Dune\"\n    assert body[0][\"author\"] == \"Frank Herbert\"\n    assert isinstance(body[0][\"id\"], int)\n\n\ndef test_listed_book_carries_exactly_id_title_and_author(web_client):\n    _add(web_client, \"Dune\", \"Frank Herbert\")\n\n    body = web_client.get(\"/books\").get_json()\n\n    assert set(body[0].keys()) == {\"id\", \"title\", \"author\"}\n\n\ndef test_several_books_are_listed_in_the_order_added(web_client):\n    for title in [\"Third-added-last\", \"A-first\", \"M-second\"]:\n        _add(web_client, title)\n\n    body = web_client.get(\"/books\").get_json()\n\n    assert [row[\"title\"] for row in body] == [\"Third-added-last\", \"A-first\", \"M-second\"]\n\n\ndef test_listed_ids_ascend_across_the_sequence(web_client):\n    for title in [\"One\", \"Two\", \"Three\", \"Four\"]:\n        _add(web_client, title)\n\n    ids = [row[\"id\"] for row in web_client.get(\"/books\").get_json()]\n\n    assert ids == sorted(ids)\n    assert len(set(ids)) == len(ids)\n\n\ndef test_book_added_after_a_listing_appears_at_the_end(web_client):\n    _add(web_client, \"First\")\n    web_client.get(\"/books\")\n    _add(web_client, \"Second\")\n\n    body = web_client.get(\"/books\").get_json()\n\n    assert [row[\"title\"] for row in body] == [\"First\", \"Second\"]\n\n\ndef test_repeated_listing_returns_the_same_sequence(web_client):\n    for title in [\"Alpha\", \"Beta\"]:\n        _add(web_client, title)\n\n    first = web_client.get(\"/books\").get_json()\n    second = web_client.get(\"/books\").get_json()\n\n    assert first == second\n\n\ndef test_rejected_submission_is_not_listed(web_client):\n    _add(web_client, \"Kept\")\n    assert web_client.post(\"/books\", data={\"title\": \"\", \"author\": \"Nobody\"}).status_code == 400\n\n    body = web_client.get(\"/books\").get_json()\n\n    assert [row[\"title\"] for row in body] == [\"Kept\"]\n\n\ndef test_listing_matches_the_persistence_store_order(web_client, store):\n    for title in [\"Store-one\", \"Store-two\", \"Store-three\"]:\n        _add(web_client, title)\n\n    http_ids = [row[\"id\"] for row in web_client.get(\"/books\").get_json()]\n    with open_database(store) as database:\n        store_ids = [row.id for row in database.books.list()]\n\n    assert http_ids == store_ids\n\n\ndef test_list_books_service_returns_rows_in_the_order_added(store):\n    with open_database(store) as database:\n        for title in An empty title or author is refused\n    without touching the store, so a stored book always has both.\n    \"\"\"\n    if not title:\n        raise BookRejected(\"rejected: title is empty\")\n    if not author:\n        raise BookRejected(\"rejected: author is empty\")\n    return database.books.create(title=title, author=author)\n\n\ndef list_books(database: Database) -> list[BookRow]:\n    \"\"\"Return every stored book in the order added, oldest first.\n\n    The order is enforced here, by ascending id, rather than trusted to the store's select, which\n    the generated persistence layer issues without an ORDER BY clause.\n    \"\"\"\n    return sorted(database.books.list(), key=lambda row: row.id)\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":14,"oldLines":6,"newStart":14,"newLines":14,"lines":["         self.reason = reason"," "," ","+class BookNotFound(LookupError):","+    \"\"\"A removal named an id that no stored book carries; ``book_id`` is that id.\"\"\"","+","+    def __init__(self, book_id: int) -> None:","+        super().__init__(book_id)","+        self.book_id = book_id","+","+"," def add_book(database: Database, title: str, author: str) -> BookRow:","     \"\"\"Store a book appended after every existing book and return the stored row."," "]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_01Mgx3qaTwhNi6k7KDW4LPyi","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}
